citation: Liquid-liquid phase separation of GPS2-LATS1 promotes colorectal cancer progression by reprogramming lipid metabolism (PMID: 40715488)
sample_size: CRC cell lines and in vivo tumor models
summary: GPS2 is overexpressed in colorectal cancer and promotes lipid metabolic reprogramming through dual regulation: facilitating SREBP1 nuclear translocation to activate lipid synthesis and increasing PPARα transcription to promote fatty acid oxidation. GPS2 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to form biomolecular condensates that interact with LATS1 kinase domain, suppressing LATS1 activity and releasing YAP to amplify lipid metabolism. GPS2 depletion inhibits tumor growth in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Nonproteolytic ubiquitination regulates chromatin occupancy by the NCoR/SMRT/HDAC3 corepressor complex in MCF-7 breast cancer cells (PMID: 40305047)
sample_size: MCF-7 breast cancer cells with genome-wide RNA-seq and ChIP-seq
summary: Nuclear GPS2 is required for licensing HDAC3 recruitment to chromatin via restricted ubiquitination by TRAF6 E3 ligase. GPS2 regulates the switch from repressive to activating functions of the NCoR/SMRT complex. TRAF6-mediated ubiquitination of TAB2 (facultative NCoR/SMRT component) contributes to corepressor clearance from target regulatory regions in response to IL-1β stimulation.

citation: GPS2-mediated regulation of the adipocyte secretome modulates adipose tissue remodeling at the onset of diet-induced obesity (PMID: 36731652)
sample_size: adipocyte-specific GPS2-KO mice with single-cell RNA-seq and proteomics
summary: Adipocyte-specific GPS2 knockout (GPS2-AKO) mice show impaired adaptation to high-fat diet, with increased inflammation, insulin resistance, and obesity compared to wildtype. Loss of GPS2 in adipocytes alters stromal cell populations and increases expression of secreted factors promoting TGFβ-driven fibrotic microenvironment. GPS2 regulates transcriptional rewiring of adipocyte-derived exosomal cargo critical for healthy tissue remodeling.

citation: ASHG 2010 - A functional analysis of GABARAP on 17p13.1 by knockdown zebrafish (T. Yamamoto et al.)
summary: GPS2 is located in the 17p13.1 microdeletion region associated with mental retardation, intractable epilepsy, and dysmorphic features. GPS2 is noted as having functional importance in neuronal development alongside DLG4/PSD95 and GABARAP. No pathogenic mutations in GPS2 were found in a cohort of 142 patients with idiopathic developmental delay with/without epilepsy.

citation: Multiple interactions recruit BLTP2 to ER-PM contacts to control plasma membrane dynamics (PMID: 40899996)
summary: BLTP2/KIAA0100 is a bridge-like lipid transfer protein that mediates bulk lipid transport between the ER and PM by tethering the ER to tubular endosomes and macropinosomes. BLTP2 binds to the PM through interactions with phosphoinositides, adaptor proteins FAM102A/FAM102B, and N-BAR domain proteins. Absence of BLTP2 results in accumulation of intracellular vacuoles connected to the PM, indicating a role in PM dynamics control.

citation: KIAA0100 Modulates Cancer Cell Aggression Behavior of MDA-MB-231 through Microtubule and Heat Shock Proteins (PMID: 29867023)
summary: KIAA0100 silencing by siRNA in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells reduced cell aggregation, reattachment, metastasis, and invasion, and sensitized quiescent cells to anoikis. KIAA0100 stabilizes microtubule structure as a microtubule-binding protein and interacts with heat shock protein HSPA1A to confer anoikis resistance.

citation: Preparation of monoclonal antibody against human KIAA0100 protein and Northern blot analysis of human KIAA0100 gene (PMID: 29404037)
summary: Northern blot analysis in U937 cells revealed that human KIAA0100 gene produces two different mRNA products (6000-10000 bp and 5000-6000 bp), and Western blot showed two protein products (254 kDa and <250 kDa), indicating alternative splicing or post-translational modification.

citation: Bioinformatic prediction and functional characterization of human KIAA0100 gene (PMID: 29404013)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated downregulation of KIAA0100 in U937 cells inhibited cell proliferation and promoted apoptosis. Bioinformatic analysis predicted KIAA0100 localizes to the secretory pathway, contains a signal peptide, transmembrane region, and four FMP27 domains. KIAA0100 is proposed as a novel anti-apoptotic factor in acute monocytic leukemia.

citation: Circ_0000520 interacts with miR-512-5p to upregulate KIAA0100 to promote malignant behaviors in lung cancer (PMID: 35866672)
summary: KIAA0100 is a target of miR-512-5p in lung cancer; the circ_0000520/miR-512-5p/KIAA0100 axis regulates lung cancer cell proliferation, cell cycle progression, migration, invasion, and angiogenesis. KIAA0100 upregulation promotes malignant behaviors in lung cancer cells.

citation: Multiple interactions mediate the localization of BLTP2 at ER-PM contacts to control plasma membrane dynamics (PMID: 39974967)
summary: BLTP2/KIAA0100 localizes at ER-PM contacts through interactions with phosphoinositides, adaptor proteins FAM102A and FAM102B, and N-BAR domain proteins. The protein mediates bulk lipid transport between ER and PM and controls PM dynamics through lipid transfer function.

citation: Identification of BCOX1, a novel gene overexpressed in breast cancer (PMID: 16289875)
summary: BCOX1 (homologous to KIAA0100) is overexpressed in breast carcinoma with mRNA signal localized to the cytoplasm of cancer epithelial cells. BCOX1 mRNA expression is moderately elevated in ductal in situ carcinoma, peaks in invasive and metastatic breast carcinoma, and is absent in benign ductal epithelial cells.

citation: Profiling the Somatic Mutational Landscape of Breast Tumors from Hispanic/Latina Women Reveals Conserved and Unique Characteristics (PMID: 37145128)
summary: Whole-exome and RNA sequencing of 146 breast tumors from Hispanic/Latina women identified a recurrent copy-number amplification at 17q11.2 associated with high KIAA0100 gene expression that has been implicated in breast cancer aggressiveness. This amplification was more prevalent in Hispanic/Latina compared to non-Hispanic White women.

citation: Bioinformatics-based modeling of lung squamous cell carcinoma prognosis and prediction of immunotherapy response (PMID: 39724502)
sample_size: Large-scale cross-platform analysis integrating GEO and TCGA databases
summary: KIAA0100 was identified as one of 11 key genes in a Cox proportional risk model for predicting lung squamous cell carcinoma patient survival and prognosis. Gene expression variations of KIAA0100 between normal and cancerous lung tissues were significantly associated with patient survival outcomes.

citation: Extended lifespan and reduced adiposity in mice lacking the FAT10 gene (PMID: 24706839)
phenotype: increased median lifespan (20%); increased overall lifespan; elevated metabolic rate; preferential use of fat as fuel; dramatically reduced adiposity; increased AMP kinase activity in skeletal muscle; increased β-oxidation in skeletal muscle; increased uncoupling in skeletal muscle; decreased triglyceride content in skeletal muscle; reduced circulating glucose levels; reduced circulating insulin levels; enhanced insulin sensitivity in metabolic tissues; elevated IL-10 in skeletal muscle and serum

citation: The ubiquitin-like modifier FAT10 is not essential for MHC-I antigen presentation (PMID: 40821782)
phenotype: no effect on MHC-I surface expression; no effect on MHC-I recovery; no effect on generation of endogenous MHC-I epitopes; no effect on generation of virus-derived MHC-I epitopes; unchanged cytotoxic T cell response to viruses compared to wild-type

citation: Single-cell profiling reveals immune disturbances landscape and HLA-F-mediated immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface in preeclampsia (PMID: 37854606)
summary: HLA-F overexpression in Jar trophoblast cells promoted cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, while underexpression had opposite effects. In NK-92MI cells, HLA-F overexpression increased secretion of immunoregulatory cytokines (CSF1, CCL22) and promoted adaptive NKG2C+ NK cell transformation.

citation: Immunity at maternal-fetal interface: KIR/HLA (Allo)recognition (PMID: 35610960)
summary: HLA-F is expressed as a non-classical HLA class I molecule on trophoblasts at the maternal-fetal interface. It functions in KIR-HLA interactions with decidual NK cells and is part of the trophoblast HLA profile (alongside HLA-C, HLA-E, HLA-G) essential for maternal immune recognition and placental establishment.

citation: A role for both HLA-F and HLA-G in reproduction and during pregnancy? (PMID: 31558330)
summary: HLA-F can be expressed as both open conformers binding to KIRs on NK cells and as peptide-bound HLA-F binding to ILT2 and ILT4 receptors. HLA-F has potential involvement in viral infections, cancer immunology, fertility, and reproduction, with possible unique roles distinct from HLA-G.

citation: HLA-F regulates the proliferation of trophoblast via PKM2-dependent glycolysis in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia (PMID: 40251569)
summary: HLA-F overexpression in Jar cells promoted PKM2 expression and enzymatic activity, enhancing glycolysis and cell proliferation. HLA-F binds the PKM promoter to regulate PKM2 transcription and suppresses lactylation of PKM2 K305 to increase enzyme activity. Reduced HLA-F expression in preeclampsia impairs trophoblast proliferation through PKM2 downregulation.

citation: Non-Classical HLA Class 1b and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (PMID: 37371767)
summary: HLA-F is a non-classical HLA-Ib molecule involved in hepatocellular carcinoma pathogenesis through interactions with innate lymphoid cell receptors on NK cells and innate lymphoid cell type 2. HLA-F-mediated NK and Vδ2 T-cell activation contributes to risk assessment and immunotherapy strategies in HCC.

citation: The involvement of HLA-E and -F in pregnancy (PMID: 16487601)
summary: HLA-F is expressed on the surface of extravillous trophoblast that has invaded the maternal decidua, a unique expression site in human development. HLA-F possesses unique receptor-ligand interactions that collectively with HLA-E and HLA-G contribute to maternal acceptance of the semi-allogeneic fetus.

citation: HLA class Ib in pregnancy and pregnancy-related disorders (PMID: 28699111)
summary: HLA-F is a non-classical HLA class Ib molecule expressed at the feto-maternal interface with immune-modulatory and tolerogenic functions. HLA-F plays a role in fertility, reproduction, and pregnancy, with potential involvement in pregnancy complications including implantation failure, recurrent spontaneous abortions, and pre-eclampsia.

citation: ASHG 2010 - Identification of multiple genetic variants related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition through genome-wide scan
sample_size: 277 NPC patients, 285 healthy controls, replicated in independent cohorts
summary: Genome-wide association study identified novel significant associations between nasopharyngeal carcinoma and HLA-F SNPs (rs3129055 and rs9258122; p = 7.36 x 10-11 and 3.33 x 10-10, respectively) in a Taiwanese population of 277 NPC patients and 285 healthy controls, with replication in independent case-control samples.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Illuminating the dark genome: Evaluation of technologies to assess medically relevant dark spots
summary: A polymorphic 2.6 kbp deletion upstream of HLA-F was identified and correlated with HLA-F expression level and exon usage in RNA-seq analysis, demonstrating regulatory variation in the HLA-F locus that affects gene expression.

citation: ASHG 2015 - Integrative analysis for identification of shared markers from various functional cells/tissues for rheumatoid arthritis
sample_size: 7 datasets from multiple RA-related tissues and cells
summary: Multi-dataset analysis identified HLA-F as a shared candidate gene in rheumatoid arthritis across multiple cell types and tissues (synovial tissue, macrophages, PBMCs). HLA-F was significant in gene-based association analysis (p=1.03E-31) and connected with known RA genes in protein-protein interaction networks.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes (PMID: not provided)
variant_detail: PTVesc (protein-truncating variant escaping nonsense-mediated decay) in HDAC2
phenotype: syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: de novo PTVesc mutations identified in 2 patients with syndromic NDD; genes with PTVesc enrichment identified through systematic analysis of 97,728 clinical exomes; high phenotypic similarity scoring

citation: ASHG 2015 - Aggregated analysis of developmental disorders reveals novel risk genes and improves genetic diagnosis (PMID: not provided)
variant_detail: de novo rare variants in HDAC2
phenotype: developmental disorder; autism; intellectual disability; epilepsy
diagnostic_reason: de novo mutations identified in aggregated analysis of 1984 patients with undiagnosed developmental disorders; HDAC2 identified as candidate risk gene with plausible mechanism in histone modification; supported by publicly available de novo mutation data from ~5500 NDD cases

citation: Early differential impact of MeCP2 mutations on functional networks in Rett syndrome patient-derived human cerebral organoids (PMID: 39149328)
phenotype: Rett syndrome; abnormal neuronal activity; altered network function
diagnostic_reason: Transcriptomic analyses revealed HDAC2-associated impairment in R306C MeCP2 organoids; functional studies in patient-derived cerebral organoids

citation: HDAC1 Regulates Neuronal Differentiation (PMID: 35095417)
phenotype: Impaired neuronal differentiation in adult hippocampus; Compromised neuronal differentiation in vitro upon viral infection-mediated deletion

citation: Histone Acetyltransferases p300 and CBP Coordinate Distinct Chromatin Remodeling Programs in Vascular Smooth Muscle Plasticity (PMID: 35502657)
phenotype: HDAC2 recruited to contractile protein promoters by CBP; Altered histone acetylation and PolII binding at contractile gene promoters; Differential regulation of vascular smooth muscle cell phenotype

citation: HRD1-mediated ubiquitination of HDAC2 regulates PPARα-mediated autophagy and alleviates metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (PMID: 38815686)
phenotype: Reduced hypoxia-suppressed autophagy in hepatocytes upon HDAC2 knockdown; Improved hepatic autophagy and reduced fatty liver disease phenotype; Reduced fibrosis and apoptosis in liver tissues

citation: HDAC2 Facilitates Pancreatic Cancer Metastasis (PMID: 34903606)
phenotype: Impaired cell cycle control in vitro; Reduced metastasis in vivo; Altered expression of prosurvival receptor tyrosine kinases (PDGFRα, PDGFRβ, EGFR); Disabled tumor-suppressive arm of TGFβ pathway

citation: Epigenetic inhibition of CTCF by HN1 promotes dedifferentiation and stemness of anaplastic thyroid cancer (PMID: 37993084)
phenotype: Reduced tumor growth in xenograft models; Loss of cancer stemness; Upregulation of thyroid differentiation markers

citation: HDAC2-mediated recruitment of METTL3 to chromatin regulates human embryonic stem cell differentiation (PMID: 41066234)
phenotype: Reduced METTL3 chromatin binding upon HDAC2 knockout; Reduced m6A levels on HDAC2 target genes linked to lineage differentiation; Significantly impaired human embryonic stem cell differentiation; Decreased RNA stability and translation of target genes

citation: PIM1-HDAC2 axis modulates intestinal homeostasis through epigenetic modification (PMID: 39027246)
sample_size: Ulcerative colitis patients and murine models
summary: HDAC2 is a direct interacting partner of PIM1 kinase in intestinal epithelial cells. PIM1 phosphorylates and downregulates HDAC2 levels, which alters epigenetic profiles of Wnt signaling pathway genes and impairs goblet cell differentiation during colitis pathogenesis.

citation: HDAC2 promotes autophagy-associated HCC malignant progression by transcriptionally activating LAPTM4B (PMID: 39147759)
summary: HDAC2 acts as a transcriptional activator that binds to the LAPTM4B promoter at four distinct sites to enhance its transcription and promote autophagy-driven hepatocellular carcinoma progression. High HDAC2 expression correlates with poor HCC prognosis and is an independent predictor of patient outcomes.

citation: N6-methyladenosine-modified SENP1, identified by IGF2BP3, is a novel molecular marker in acute myeloid leukemia and aggravates progression by activating AKT signal via de-SUMOylating HDAC2 (PMID: 38822351)
sample_size: AML patient datasets (OHSU, TCGA, TARGET, MILE)
summary: HDAC2 is a direct substrate of SENP1 deSUMOylase. SENP1 removes SUMO modifications from HDAC2, which enhances EGFR transcription and activates the AKT/mTOR signaling pathway to promote AML proliferation and anti-apoptosis.

citation: YTHDC1 is downregulated by the YY1/HDAC2 complex and controls the sensitivity of ccRCC to sunitinib by targeting the ANXA1-MAPK pathway (PMID: 35974388)
summary: HDAC2 functions as part of a YY1/HDAC2 transcriptional repressor complex that downregulates YTHDC1 expression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma. This axis modulates sensitivity to tyrosine kinase inhibitors through the ANXA1/MAPK pathway, and HDAC2 inhibitors can resensitize resistant tumors.

citation: HDAC2 Facilitates Pancreatic Cancer Metastasis (PMID: 34903606)
summary: HDAC2 is a cellular fitness factor that controls cell cycle progression and metastatic dissemination in undifferentiated, mesenchymal pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. HDAC2 maintains expression of prosurvival receptor tyrosine kinases (PDGFRα, PDGFRβ, EGFR) and disables the tumor-suppressive TGFβ pathway.

citation: Damascenone inhibits osteoclastogenesis by epigenetically modulating Nrf2-mediated ROS scavenge and counteracts OVX-induced osteoporosis (PMID: 39547093)
summary: HDAC2 is identified as a direct target of the natural compound damascenone. Damascenone inhibits HDAC2 function and increases H3K27ac histone acetylation at the Nrf2 promoter, inducing Nrf2 expression and ROS scavenging to suppress osteoclastogenesis in vitro and in vivo.

citation: HRD1-mediated ubiquitination of HDAC2 regulates PPARα-mediated autophagy and alleviates metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (PMID: 38815686)
summary: HDAC2 is a substrate of the E3 ubiquitin ligase HRD1 and acts as a transcriptional repressor of PPARα. HRD1-mediated ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation of HDAC2 relieves PPARα repression and promotes hepatic autophagy to alleviate hypoxia-induced metabolic-associated fatty liver disease.

citation: Emerging roles and therapeutic implications of HDAC2 and IL-17A in steroid-resistant asthma (PMID: 39170824)
sample_size: Severe asthma and smoking-induced asthma patients
summary: HDAC2 activity is significantly reduced in patients with severe asthma and smoking-induced asthma, leading to increased acetylation of glucocorticoid receptors and amplified expression of inflammatory genes. Restoring HDAC2 activity is proposed as a therapeutic approach to reverse steroid insensitivity.

citation: Histone deacetylase-mediated silencing of PSTPIP2 expression contributes to aristolochic acid nephropathy-induced PANoptosis (PMID: 38073114)
sample_size: Mouse kidney and renal tubular epithelial cells
summary: HDAC2 expression is upregulated in aristolochic acid-induced kidney injury and mediates transcriptional silencing of PSTPIP2. HDAC1/HDAC2-specific inhibitor romidepsin suppresses aristolochic acid-induced PANoptosis (pyroptosis, apoptosis, necroptosis) by upregulating PSTPIP2 and regulating caspase 8.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes
summary: HDAC2 was identified as a candidate gene for neurodevelopmental disorders through systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay-escaping protein-truncating variants. Two patients with syndromic neurodevelopmental delay carried de novo PTVesc mutations in HDAC2, suggesting loss-of-function variants in this histone modifier cause developmental disease.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Large-scale trans-ethnic genome-wide association study reveals novel loci, causal molecular mechanisms and effector genes for kidney function
significance: p < 5×10⁻⁸ for multiple loci; enrichment analysis p < 0.00039
summary: HDAC2 binding sites are significantly enriched in eGFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) association signals across 312,468 individuals of diverse ancestry. Class I histone deacetylases including HDAC2 are required for embryonic kidney gene expression, growth and differentiation.

citation: The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment (PMID: 32572597)
phenotype: Elevated static level of DRD2 protein in pituitary gland; Elevated static level of DRD2 protein in thalamus; Elevated static level of DRD2 protein in heart

citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (PMID: 33990333)
phenotype: Defective convergent extension during gastrulation; Impaired Wnt/planar cell polarity signaling

citation: MicroRNA-21 prevents excessive inflammation and cardiac dysfunction after myocardial infarction through targeting KBTBD7 (PMID: 29991775)
phenotype: Enhanced p38 and NF-κB signaling activation in cardiac tissue post myocardial infarction; Promoted DAMP-triggered inflammatory responses in macrophages; Interaction with MKK3/6 and promotion of their activation

citation: Mutations of RNF213 are responsible for sporadic cerebral cavernous malformation and lead to a mulberry-like cluster in zebrafish (PMID: 32248732)
phenotype: Downregulation of kbtbd7 expression in rnf213a mutants; Mulberry-like cluster of disordered-flow vascular channels phenotype partly rescued by kbtbd7 mRNA

citation: The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment (PMID: 32572597)
sample_size: KBTBD7 KO mice generated; human pituitary tumors analyzed
significance: KBTBD7 expression negatively correlated with DRD2 in human pituitary tumors; highly expressed in dopamine-resistant prolactinomas
summary: KBTBD7 was identified as a DRD2-interacting protein via yeast two-hybrid screening. KBTBD6/7 directly interacts with and ubiquitinates DRD2 at five specific lysine residues (K221, K226, K241, K251, K258), promoting proteasome-mediated degradation of DRD2. KBTBD7 knockout mice showed elevated DRD2 protein levels in pituitary, thalamus, and heart.

citation: KBTBD7 promotes non-small cell lung carcinoma progression by enhancing ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PTEN (PMID: 35499228)
sample_size: 102 paired NSCLC and peritumoral normal specimens
significance: KBTBD7 expression positively correlated with histological type, P-TNM stage, lymph node metastasis, and tumor size
summary: KBTBD7 was highly expressed in NSCLC tissues and cell lines. KBTBD7 knockdown inhibited NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion. KBTBD7 enhanced ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PTEN, activating EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling and regulating downstream effectors including CCNE1, CDK4, P27, ZEB-1, Claudin-1, ROCK1, MMP-9, and E-cadherin.

citation: CUL3-KBTBD6/KBTBD7 ubiquitin ligase cooperates with GABARAP proteins to spatially restrict TIAM1-RAC1 signaling (PMID: 25684205)
sample_size: Zebrafish gastrulation model; breast cancer cells
significance: KBTBD6/7 depletion leads to elevated RAC1 activity, loss of focal adhesions, reduced proliferation, and enhanced invasion
summary: KBTBD6/7 are substrate adaptors for a CUL3 RING ubiquitin ligase complex that mediates ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of TIAM1, a RAC1-specific GEF. KBTBD6/7 employ ATG8-interacting motifs to bind GABARAP proteins, and TIAM1 ubiquitylation depends on GABARAP binding. KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation and functions as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer.

citation: Crocin inhibits KBTBD7 to prevent excessive inflammation and cardiac dysfunction following myocardial infarction (PMID: 36484363)
significance: Crocin-treated groups showed significantly decreased IL-1β, IL-6, and TNFα levels compared to model group
summary: KBTBD7 was identified as a direct target of crocin. KBTBD7 knockdown significantly inhibited p38 and NF-κB signaling pathways and reduced production of inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNFα) induced by rmHMGB1 and rmHSP60 in RAW264.7 cells. In vivo, crocin treatment reduced myocardial apoptosis and inflammatory cytokine levels in a rat myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury model.

citation: Knockdown of KBTBD7 attenuates septic lung injury by inhibiting ferroptosis and improving mitochondrial dysfunction (PMID: 38652964)
sample_size: Human alveolar epithelial cells; septic lung injury mice
significance: KBTBD7 knockdown significantly reduced pro-inflammatory factors and ROS production in vitro and in vivo
summary: KBTBD7 was highly expressed in LPS-induced human alveolar epithelial cells. KBTBD7 knockdown reduced inflammatory response, ROS production, ferroptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, KBTBD7 interacts with FOXA1, promotes FOXA1 expression, and indirectly inhibits SLC7A11 transcription. In vivo, KBTBD7 knockdown improved lung tissue damage in septic lung injury mice.

citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (PMID: 33990333)
significance: KBTBD7 regulates Wnt/PCP signaling through ERAD pathway; functions as tumor suppressor
summary: KBTBD7 is recruited by p97/VCP via UBA-UBX adaptors to promote Vangl ubiquitination and ERAD. Wnt5a/CK1 prevents Vangl ubiquitination by inducing Vangl phosphorylation, facilitating ER export. KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation and functions as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer by promoting Vangl degradation.

citation: Targeting of ubiquitination and degradation of KLF15 by E3 ubiquitin ligase KBTBD7 regulates LPS-induced septic brain injury in microglia (PMID: 39489209)
sample_size: Rat CLP septic brain injury model; primary microglia
significance: KBTBD7 knockdown markedly inhibited LPS-induced proinflammatory cytokine release and inflammasome activation
summary: KBTBD7 expression was upregulated in a rat cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) septic brain injury model and in LPS-treated primary microglia. Co-IP confirmed KBTBD7 as a novel interacting protein of KLF15 transcription factor. KBTBD7 acts as an E3 ubiquitin ligase catalyzing KLF15 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. KBTBD7 knockdown inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome and NF-κB signaling activation.

citation: New TFII-I family target genes involved in embryonic development (PMID: 19527686)
sample_size: Mouse embryos with targeted disruption of Gtf2i and Gtf2ird1
significance: KBTBD7 significantly down-regulated in TFII-I mutant embryos; potential role in Williams syndrome etiology
summary: KBTBD7 (1110008P08Rik) encodes an adapter protein with BTB/POZ, BACK, and Kelch motifs. Microarray analysis revealed KBTBD7 was dramatically down-regulated in Gtf2i and Gtf2ird1 mutant embryos. KBTBD7 possesses well-conserved TFII-I-binding consensus sites in its proximal promoter, suggesting it is a direct target of TFII-I transcription factors. Based on expression pattern, KBTBD7 may have a specific role in brain development and function.

citation: MicroRNA-21 prevents excessive inflammation and cardiac dysfunction after myocardial infarction through targeting KBTBD7 (PMID: 29991775)
sample_size: miR-21 knockout and WT mice; macrophages treated with DAMPs
significance: miR-21 knockout mice had significantly higher inflammatory cytokine levels and worse cardiac outcomes post-MI
summary: miR-21 directly targets KBTBD7 to suppress inflammatory responses post-MI. KBTBD7 interacts with MKK3/6 and promotes their activation, enhancing p38 and NF-κB signaling. miR-21 knockout mice showed decreased survival, worse cardiac dysfunction, increased infarct areas, and elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) after MI. miR-21 overexpression markedly inhibited DAMP-triggered inflammatory cytokine production in macrophages.

citation: Berberine reduces inflammation of human dental pulp fibroblast via miR-21/KBTBD7 axis (PMID: 31837588)
significance: Berberine (25 μM) treatment reduced IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α expression and enhanced cell proliferation via miR-21/KBTBD7 axis
summary: In LPS-induced human dental pulp fibroblasts, KBTBD7 expression was upregulated while miR-21 was downregulated. miR-21 negatively targets KBTBD7 via direct binding (confirmed by luciferase reporter assay). Berberine treatment upregulated miR-21 and downregulated KBTBD7, reducing inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and inhibiting NF-κB signaling activation. miR-21 overexpression or KBTBD7 silencing enhanced berberine's protective effects.

citation: ASHG 2015 - The Koolen-de Vries syndrome: A phenotypic comparison of microdeletion and point mutation patients (Koolen et al.)
variant_detail: KANSL1 point mutations (specific variants not detailed in abstract)
phenotype: neonatal hypotonia; developmental delay; moderate intellectual disability; characteristic facial dysmorphism; epilepsy; musculoskeletal anomalies; congenital heart defects; urogenital malformations; ectodermal anomalies; expressive language delay; social and friendly behavior
diagnostic_reason: Truncating mutations in KANSL1 cause Koolen-de Vries syndrome; haploinsufficiency of KANSL1 is sufficient to cause full KdVS phenotype
center_country: Multiple European centers (DDD Study, KdVS research group)

citation: Kansl1 haploinsufficiency impairs autophagosome-lysosome fusion and links autophagic dysfunction with Koolen-de Vries syndrome in mice (PMID: 35177641)
diagnostic_reason: Mouse model study (Kansl1+/- mice); not human patient data

variant_detail: KANSL1 loss-of-function (patient-derived iPSCs and genome-edited lines)
phenotype: Koolen-de Vries Syndrome; intellectual disability; reduced synaptic density; reduced AMPA receptor-mediated transmission; impaired neuronal network activity; oxidative stress; autophagosome accumulation
diagnostic_reason: KANSL1-deficient human iPSCs from KdVS patients; loss-of-function strongly associated with KdVS

phenotype: extraembryonic ectoderm abnormalities; embryonic lethality; impaired trophoblast self-renewal; reduced CDX2 expression; decreased H4K16ac levels

citation: Histone acetyltransferase KAT8 is essential for mouse oocyte development by regulating reactive oxygen species levels (PMID: 28506985)
phenotype: female infertility; follicle development failure at secondary and preantral stages; downregulation of antioxidant genes; increased reactive oxygen species; defective oocyte development

citation: Role of Activin A-Mediated KAT8 Expression in Regulating Ferroptosis During Mycobacterium tuberculosis Infection (PMID: 40976643)
phenotype: reduced Mycobacterium tuberculosis burden; limited bacterial dissemination; ameliorated tuberculosis pathology; altered NRF2 nuclear localization; decreased HO-1 expression

citation: KAT8 Knockdown Reverses hucMSC Senescence and Enhances Diabetic Wound Healing Efficacy (PMID: 40816295)
phenotype: enhanced wound closure in diabetic mice; improved tissue healing; reduced senescence markers in transplanted cells; enhanced cell proliferation and migration

citation: Fto-mediated m(6)A modification is essential for cerebellar development through regulating epigenetic reprogramming (PMID: 40883822)
phenotype: cerebellar ataxia; tremors; abnormal gait patterns; increased TUJ1 expression; reduced neuronal functional genes (Map2); reduced self-renewal genes (Sox2, Sox9, Nestin, Pax6); upregulation of KAT8; altered H4K16ac modification; impaired chromatin accessibility in neural developmental pathways

citation: Mitochondrial MOF regulates energy metabolism in heart failure via ATP5B hyperacetylation (PMID: 39392752)
phenotype: mitochondrial dysfunction; cardiac remodeling; heart failure; impaired mitochondrial respiration; altered energy metabolism; ATP5B hyperacetylation at K201

citation: KAT8 catalyzes the acetylation of SEPP1 at lysine 247/249 and modulates the activity of CD8(+) T cells via LRP8 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 39972392)
phenotype: reduced pancreatic tumor growth; reduced liver metastasis; altered CD8+ T cell abundance; altered MDSC abundance; enhanced anti-PD-1 therapy efficacy

citation: KAT8-catalyzed lactylation promotes eEF1A2-mediated protein synthesis and colorectal carcinogenesis (PMID: 38359291)
summary: KAT8 acts as a pan-lysine lactylation (Kla) writer enzyme that catalyzes lactylation of eEF1A2 at K408, promoting translation elongation and protein synthesis in colorectal cancer. KAT8 deletion inhibits CRC tumor growth, particularly in high-lactic tumor microenvironments.

citation: Acetylation in the regulation of autophagy (PMID: 35435793)
summary: KAT8/MOF is identified as a lysine acetyltransferase involved in acetylation-mediated regulation of autophagy pathways, including regulation of core autophagy components and transcriptional control via histone acetylation.

citation: Disrupting the phase separation of KAT8-IRF1 diminishes PD-L1 expression and promotes antitumor immunity (PMID: 36894639)
summary: KAT8 undergoes phase separation with IRF1 in response to interferon-γ to form biomolecular condensates that promote IRF1 K78 acetylation and PD-L1 transcription. A blocking peptide (2142-R8) disrupts KAT8-IRF1 condensate formation and enhances antitumor immunity in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Targeting the KAT8/YEATS4 Axis Represses Tumor Growth and Increases Cisplatin Sensitivity in Bladder Cancer (PMID: 38526153)
summary: KAT8-mediated acetylation of YEATS4 prevents its ubiquitination and degradation by HUWE1 E3 ligase. High KAT8 and YEATS4 levels correlate with poor overall survival in bladder cancer patients; KAT8 inhibitor MG149 reduces YEATS4 acetylation and sensitizes BC cells to cisplatin.

citation: KAT8-mediated H4K16ac is essential for sustaining trophoblast self-renewal and proliferation via regulating CDX2 (PMID: 38961108)
summary: KAT8 is a MYST family histone acetyltransferase that acetylates H4K16 to activate CDX2 transcription, essential for trophoblast stem cell self-renewal. Kat8 knockout in trophoblasts causes extraembryonic ectoderm abnormalities and embryonic lethality; reduced KAT8, CDX2, and H4K16ac expression associates with recurrent pregnancy loss.

citation: Lysine butyrylation of HSP90 regulated by KAT8 and HDAC11 confers chemoresistance (PMID: 37460462)
summary: KAT8 acts as a writer enzyme for lysine butyrylation (Kbu) of HSP90 at K754, promoting HSP90 overexpression and 5-FU chemoresistance in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. HDAC11 serves as the eraser; SDCBP increases Kbu stability of HSP90 by competitively binding HDAC11.

citation: Epigenetic regulation of autophagy-related genes: Implications for neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 37674294)
summary: KAT8 is identified as a chromatinopathy gene that regulates transcriptional expression of autophagy-related genes, with potential implications for neurodevelopmental disorders. KAT8 is part of the NSL complex (via KANSL1 interaction) and may regulate autophagy as a key hub mechanism in NDD-related chromatinopathies.

citation: Lactate triggers KAT8-mediated LTBP1 lactylation at lysine 752 to promote skin rejuvenation by inducing collagen synthesis in fibroblasts (PMID: 39102921)
summary: KAT8 catalyzes lysine lactylation of LTBP1 at K752 in response to lactate uptake via MCT1, promoting collagen I and III synthesis in fibroblasts. This mechanism underlies PLLA-induced skin rejuvenation and demonstrates KAT8's role in lactylation of non-histone proteins.

citation: KAT8 acetylation-controlled lipolysis affects the invasive and migratory potential of colorectal cancer cells (PMID: 36849520)
summary: KAT8 itself is acetylated at K168/175 residues by GCN5 and deacetylated by SIRT6. KAT8 acetylation attenuates its binding activity and inhibits recruitment of RNA Pol II to lipolysis genes (ATGL, HSL), downregulating lipolysis and affecting invasive/migratory potential in colorectal cancer cells.

citation: ASHG 2019 - Variant-to-gene mapping for Alzheimer's disease using 3D genomics in an activated microglia human cell line (PgmNr 3267)
summary: KAT8 was identified as a putative effector gene for an Alzheimer's disease GWAS locus through Capture C promoter contactome analysis in interferon-γ activated human microglia cells, suggesting a role in AD-relevant immune activation pathways.

citation: ASHG 2015 - De novo truncating mutations MSL3 cause a new recognizable syndrome

citation: DNA double-strand break-capturing nuclear envelope tubules drive DNA repair (PMID: 38632359)
summary: KIF5B is a kinesin motor protein that collaborates with the LINC complex, NPC protein NUP153, nuclear lamina, and KIF13B to generate DSB-capturing nuclear envelope tubules (dsbNETs) that promote DNA repair and cell survival in response to DNA double-strand breaks.

citation: Mechanisms of electroacupuncture-induced neuroprotection in acute stroke rats: the role of astrocyte-mediated mitochondrial transfer (PMID: 40598228)
summary: KIF5b is identified as a protein associated with tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) involved in mitochondrial transfer from astrocytes to neurons. Electroacupuncture regulates KIF5b expression as part of a mechanism that facilitates mitochondrial transfer and provides neuroprotection during acute ischemic stroke in rats.

citation: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound improves myocardial ischaemia‒reperfusion injury via migrasome-mediated mitocytosis (PMID: 38951127)
summary: KIF5B is a mitochondrial motor protein transcriptionally activated by YAP nuclear translocation downstream of the RhoA/Myosin II/F-actin pathway. KIF5B is essential for LIPUS-induced migrasome-dependent mitocytosis and removal of damaged mitochondria during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice.

citation: A dual role of ERGIC-localized Rabs in TMED10-mediated unconventional protein secretion (PMID: 38926505)
summary: KIF5B collaborates with Rab2A to regulate ERGIC compartmentalization and establish a UcPS-specific compartment, governing cargo translocation and specifying the ERGIC's function in unconventional protein secretion.

citation: The cohesin-associated protein Pds5A governs the meiotic spindle assembly via deubiquitination of Kif5B in oocytes (PMID: 40215310)
summary: Pds5A recruits deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific protease 14 to stabilize kinesin family member 5B (Kif5B) on the spindle apparatus, regulating spindle elongation and meiotic spindle assembly during oocyte maturation. Pds5A depletion or genetic ablation leads to defects in spindle organization and compromised female fertility.

citation: Endophilin A2 controls touch and mechanical allodynia via kinesin-mediated Piezo2 trafficking (PMID: 38475827)
sample_size: Male and female C57BL/6 mice (8-12 weeks) and male cynomolgus monkeys (7-10 years old)
summary: KIF5B is a kinesin motor protein that interacts with EndoA2 adaptor protein to mediate membrane trafficking of the mechanically sensitive ion channel Piezo2 in dorsal root ganglion neurons. The KIF5B/EndoA2/Piezo2 complex is essential for Piezo2 trafficking and sustaining touch and mechanical pain signal transmission in mice and nonhuman primates.

citation: Inhibition of KIF5b-mediated Nav1.8 transport by ropivacaine contributes to axonal regeneration following sciatic nerve injury in rats (PMID: 39332671)
summary: KIF5b mediates axonal transport of the voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.8 from dorsal root ganglia to the lesion site following peripheral nerve injury. KIF5b overexpression impairs axonal regrowth, reduces macrophage infiltration and myelin debris clearance, and delays functional recovery; ropivacaine promotes axonal regeneration by inhibiting KIF5b-mediated Nav1.8 forward transport.

sample_size: HCC cell lines and xenograft mouse model
summary: CircCCAR1 acts as a molecular sponge to sequester miR-641, relieving miR-641-mediated inhibition of KIF5B mRNA, and directly binds to PTBP1 which stabilizes KIF5B mRNA. KIF5B upregulation promotes HCC cell proliferation; silencing circCCAR1 suppresses HCC progression through the miR-641/KIF5B axis in cell culture and xenograft mouse models.

citation: KLF7 regulates super-enhancer-driven IGF2BP2 overexpression to promote the progression of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 38443991)
summary: KLF7 acts as a transcription factor that directly binds to the promoter and super-enhancer regions of IGF2BP2 to induce its transcription. KLF7 expression positively correlates with IGF2BP2 abundance in HNSCC, and patients with high expression of both genes show poorer prognosis. Mechanistic studies used ChIP-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assays to demonstrate direct KLF7-DNA binding.

citation: HMGB1-mediated elevation of KLF7 facilitates hepatocellular carcinoma progression and metastasis through upregulating TLR4 and PTK2 (PMID: 37554278)
summary: KLF7 functions as a transcriptional activator that directly transactivates TLR4 and PTK2 expression. HMGB1 upregulates KLF7 through the TLR4/RAGE-PI3K-AKT-NF-κB pathway, forming a positive feedback loop. KLF7 expression correlates with cytoplasmic HMGB1, p-p65, TLR4, and PTK2 levels in human HCC samples.

citation: KLF7-regulated ITGA2 as a therapeutic target for inhibiting oral cancer stem cells (PMID: 40316546)
summary: KLF7 directly regulates ITGA2 expression by binding to its promoter, as demonstrated by chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing and dual-luciferase assays. KLF7 maintains cancer stem cell stemness in OSCC through ITGA2-mediated activation of PI3K-AKT, MAPK, and Hippo signaling pathways upon collagen binding.

citation: KLF7 Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression Through Regulating SLC1A5-Mediated Tryptophan Metabolism (PMID: 39648156)
summary: KLF7 acts as a transcriptional activator that directly binds to the promoter of SLC1A5 to upregulate its expression. KLF7 promotes HCC progression by regulating tryptophan metabolism through SLC1A5-mediated uptake, with downstream effects on serotonin production and cell proliferation/migration.

citation: KLF7 promotes colon adenocarcinoma progression through the PDGFB signaling pathway (PMID: 38164176)
summary: KLF7 specifically binds to the PDGFB promoter region (TGGGTGGAG motif) to promote PDGFB transcription and secretion. Secreted PDGFB activates MAPK/ERK, PI3K/AKT, and JAK/STAT3 signaling through PDGFRβ to drive COAD progression. KLF7 overexpression correlates with clinicopathological features of COAD.

citation: KLF7 promotes neuroblastoma differentiation through the GTPase signaling pathway by upregulating neuroblast differentiation-associated protein AHNAKs and glycerophosphodiesterase GDPD5 (PMID: 38924469)
sample_size: Neuroblastoma cell lines and clinical samples
summary: KLF7 is a neuroblastoma super-enhancer-associated transcription factor that promotes neuroblastoma differentiation independently of and cooperatively with retinoic acid. KLF7 directly binds to promoters of AHNAK, AHNAK2, and GDPD5 to regulate their expression and alter GTPase activity. High KLF7 expression is associated with favorable clinical outcomes in neuroblastoma.

citation: KLF7 is associated with poor prognosis and regulates migration and adhesion in tongue cancer (PMID: 33393169)
sample_size: 127 TSCC samples from public database; 21 tongue cancer samples
summary: KLF7 is upregulated in TSCC and promotes cell migration and adhesion. RNA-seq and KEGG pathway analysis revealed that KLF7-altered genes are enriched in extracellular matrix-receptor interactions and focal adhesion pathways. KLF7 expression correlates with T and N stages and is associated with worse overall survival.

citation: KLF7 promotes adipocyte inflammation and glucose metabolism disorder by activating the PKCζ/NF-κB pathway (PMID: 37342904)
sample_size: 3T3-L1 adipocytes; HEK-293T cells; mouse adipose tissue
summary: KLF7 upregulates PKCζ expression through direct promoter binding (confirmed by luciferase reporter and ChIP assays) and activates the PKCζ/NF-κB pathway to promote IL-6 expression in adipocytes. KLF7, PKCζ, p-IκB, p-p65, and IL-6 expression are significantly increased in epididymal white adipose tissue of high-fat diet-fed mice and decreased in KLF7 fat conditional knockout mice.

citation: Expression and Clinical Significance of Serum Krüppel-Like Factor 7 (KLF7) in NSCLC Patients (PMID: 35936369)
summary: Serum KLF7 levels are significantly elevated in NSCLC patients compared to healthy controls and correlate with tumor differentiation degree and TNM stage. Cox regression analysis identified KLF7 as an independent risk factor for 3-year recurrence and metastasis in NSCLC patients, independent of gender, age, smoking history, and tumor diameter.

citation: KLF7 promotes progression of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma by remodeling tumor immune microenvironment (PMID: 41482204)
sample_size: HNSCC clinical samples and cell lines
summary: KLF7 is an oncogenic transcription factor that directly transactivates LOX expression in HNSCC cells. KLF7-driven LOX expression promotes extracellular matrix crosslinking to create a stiff microenvironment that recruits tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), which suppress CD8+ T cell-mediated killing. The KLF7/LOX/TAM axis represents a therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.

citation: ASHG 2016 - De novo alterations in KLF7 are a novel cause of intellectual disability, psychiatric and neuromuscular issues
summary: De novo missense mutations in KLF7 (p.T137M, p.P139S in F-box motif; p.D264N in zinc finger DNA-binding domain) cause intellectual disability, developmental delay, abnormal muscle tone, feeding/swallowing issues, and psychiatric features. KLF7 is implicated in neurogenesis, axon guidance, and skeletal muscle differentiation based on mouse and in vitro studies.

sample_size: clinical primary and recurrent glioma samples
significance: associated with recurrence and poor prognosis
summary: MAEA functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets PHD3 at K159 for K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation, leading to HIF-1α stabilization and enhanced stemness and temozolomide resistance in glioblastoma cells. High MAEA expression correlates with glioma recurrence and poor prognosis.

citation: Pathogenic variants in MAEA disrupt DNA replication fork stability and are associated with developmental abnormalities in humans (PMID: 40880485)
significance: disease-linked variants (R34C, E349G, Y394D, M396R) show defective replication stress response
summary: MAEA is a core component of the CTLH E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that regulates homologous recombination by mediating ubiquitylation of Ku80, enabling its removal from replication fork ends and facilitating RAD51 loading. citation: The E3 ubiquitin ligase MAEA promotes macrophage phagocytosis and inhibits gastrointestinal cancer progression by mediating PARP1 ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 39990651)

citation: The CTLH ubiquitin ligase substrates ZMYND19 and MKLN1 negatively regulate mTORC1 at the lysosomal membrane (PMID: 41315365)

MAEA knockout in EBV-associated gastric carcinoma cells synergistically blocks proliferation when combined with PI3K inhibition.

citation: MAEA is an E3 ubiquitin ligase promoting autophagy and maintenance of haematopoietic stem cells (PMID: 33947846)

MAEA deletion impairs HSC quiescence and causes lethal myeloproliferative syndrome by stabilizing cytokine receptors (MPL, FLT3) and impairing autophagy flux. MAEA restricts cytokine receptor signaling via autophagy-mediated degradation.

phenotype: enhanced LFA-1 activation on CD8 T cells; increased CD8 T cell priming; enhanced antigen-dependent activation; increased proliferation and cytokine production; enhanced cytotoxic activity; impaired tumor growth; improved response to viral infection; tolerated in adult animals under homeostatic conditions

phenotype: impaired Hippo pathway responses to external cues; undermined RhoA GTPase inhibition responses; impaired actin cytoskeleton remodeling responses; reduced LATS1/2 activation; differential regulation of actin and microtubule networks; reduced sensitivity to Taxol-mediated LATS1/2 activation

citation: Abrogation of MAP4K4 protein function causes congenital anomalies in humans and zebrafish (PMID: 37126546)
summary: MAP4K4 negatively regulates RAS signaling in early embryos. Loss-of-function and dominant-negative variants in MAP4K4 cause developmental defects in zebrafish models and are associated with neurodevelopmental differences and multiple congenital anomalies in 21 human families.

citation: RAP2 mediates mechanoresponses of the Hippo pathway (PMID: 30135582)
summary: MAP4K4 is a direct effector of RAP2 GTPase in mechanotransduction. Active RAP2 binds to and stimulates MAP4K4 (along with MAP4K6, MAP4K7, and ARHGAP29), resulting in activation of LATS1/LATS2 and inhibition of YAP/TAZ in response to ECM stiffness signals.

citation: MAP4K4 exacerbates cardiac microvascular injury in diabetes by facilitating S-nitrosylation modification of Drp1 (PMID: 38724987)
summary: MAP4K4 is upregulated in diabetic cardiomyopathy and promotes S-nitrosylation of Drp1 in cardiac microvascular endothelial cells by inhibiting GPX4 expression, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and endothelial ferroptosis. MAP4K4 inhibition via DMX-5804 reduced ferroptosis and improved cardiac dysfunction in db/db mice.

citation: MAP4K4 aggravates microvascular anomalies in diabetic retinopathy in a YTHDF2-dependent manner (PMID: 40072537)
summary: MAP4K4 is predominantly expressed in retinal endothelial cells with elevated expression in fibrovascular membranes from individuals with proliferative diabetic retinopathy compared to normal retinas. MAP4K4 regulates endothelial cell dysfunction through NF-κB signaling, and its expression is regulated by YTHDF2-mediated mRNA stability.

citation: MAP4K4 and cancer: ready for the main stage? (PMID: 37223681)
summary: MAP4K4 is a serine/threonine kinase that activates pro-proliferative pathways including JNK and MLK3, stimulates tumor cell proliferation and invasion, and alters cytoskeleton/actin function. MAP4K4 knockout is embryonic lethal due to impaired somite development, and inhibition reduces tumor proliferation, migration, and invasion in pancreatic cancer, glioblastoma, and medulloblastoma.

citation: The molecular basis of the dichotomous functionality of MAP4K4 in proliferation and cell motility control in cancer (PMID: 36568222)
summary: MAP4K4 functions as an upstream integrator of extracellular cues with dual roles: as an activator of JNK signaling promoting proliferation and cell motility, and as an activator of the Hippo tumor suppressor pathway. MAP4K4 regulates cytoskeleton dynamics and is implicated in both pro-metastatic and tumor-suppressive functions depending on context.

citation: MAP4K4: an emerging therapeutic target in cancer (PMID: 27800153)
summary: MAP4K4 is a serine/threonine kinase member of the Ste20p family with roles in immunity, inflammation, metabolic and cardiovascular disease. MAP4K4 plays important roles in cancer initiation and progression, and MAP4K4-specific inhibitors have been recently developed as potential therapeutic agents.

citation: MAP4K4 and WT1 mediate SOX6-induced cellular senescence by synergistically activating the ATF2-TGFβ2-Smad2/3 signaling pathway in cervical cancer (PMID: 38383842)
summary: MAP4K4 promotes TGFB2 gene expression through the MAP4K4-MAPK (JNK/ERK/p38)-ATF2 pathway, working synergistically with WT1 to mediate SOX6-induced cellular senescence in cervical cancer cells. This axis represents a therapeutic target for improving chemosensitivity.

citation: Histone lactylation-derived LINC01127 promotes the self-renewal of glioblastoma stem cells via the cis-regulating the MAP4K4 to activate JNK pathway (PMID: 38084701)
summary: The lncRNA LINC01127 regulates MAP4K4 expression in cis by directly guiding POLR2A to MAP4K4 promoter regions, leading to JNK pathway activation and promotion of glioblastoma stem cell self-renewal. Targeting the LINC01127-MAP4K4/JNK/NF-κB axis impeded orthotopic tumor growth in GBM xenografts.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Variants in MAP4K4 cause a novel and potentially treatable form of neurologic dysfunction with cardiac anomalies
summary: MAP4K4 is an activator of the JNK pathway controlling proliferation, embryonic development, and apoptosis. Seven individuals from four families with MAP4K4 variants show neurologic dysfunction and cardiac anomalies resembling rasopathy. MAP4K4 loss can be mitigated by inhibition of Integrin α5β1, suggesting a potential targeted therapy.

citation: Molecular cloning, sequence identification and expression analysis of novel caprine MYLPF gene (PMID: 23277391)
summary: MYLPF mRNA is highly expressed in skeletal muscles (longissimus dorsi, gastrocnemius, abdominal muscle) with lower expression in non-muscle tissues (liver, spleen, lung, kidney). citation: Mutations in MYLPF Cause a Novel Segmental Amyoplasia that Manifests as Distal Arthrogryposis (PMID: 32707087)
summary: MYLPF mutations (dominant and recessive variants) cause distal arthrogryposis with congenital contractures and segmental amyoplasia (complete absence of skeletal muscle in affected limbs). Zebrafish mylpfa knockout shows reduced trunk contractile force, complete pectoral fin paralysis, and reduced myosin activity with fiber degeneration, demonstrating that MYLPF impairment most severely affects limb movement.

citation: EPA and DHA Inhibit Myogenesis and Downregulate the Expression of Muscle-related Genes in C2C12 Myoblasts (PMID: 30669396)
summary: MYLPF (myosin light chain phosphorylatable fast skeletal muscle) expression is significantly downregulated in C2C12 myoblasts treated with EPA or DHA (50 μM), as identified by RNA-sequencing. This downregulation occurs alongside suppression of myoblast differentiation and decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and Akt signaling.

citation: Quantitative proteomic and phosphoproteomic analysis of chicken skeletal muscle during embryonic development (PMID: 34236285)
sample_size: Chicken embryonic leg muscle at 4 developmental timepoints
summary: MYLPF is identified as a phosphorylated differentially expressed protein (phospho-DEP) in chicken leg muscle during embryonic development (E7, E12, E17, D3). MYLPF interacts with troponin proteins (TNNC1, TNNC2, TNNT2, TNNT3) in focal adhesion pathways during skeletal muscle development.

citation: Identification of Potential Biomarkers for Ryanodine Receptor 1 (RYR1) Mutation-Associated Myopathies Using Bioinformatics Approach (PMID: 35692882)

summary: MYLPF is identified as a skeletal muscle tissue-specific hub gene and potential biomarker for RYR1 mutation-associated myopathies with AUC of 0.786. MYLPF is part of protein-protein interaction networks involved in muscle contraction, actin-mediated cell contraction, and actin filament-based movement pathways.

citation: Understanding Myoblast Differentiation Pathways When Cultured on Electroactive Scaffolds through Proteomic Analysis (PMID: 35635507)
sample_size: C2C12 cells differentiated on PVDF scaffolds
summary: MYLPF is highly expressed during C2C12 myoblast differentiation on piezoelectric polymer films with negative surface charge (189% upregulation), and is involved in calcium-related signaling and muscle contraction pathways. MYLPF expression is modulated by scaffold surface charge during myoblast differentiation.

citation: Fast-twitch myofibrils grow in proportion to Mylpf dosage in the zebrafish embryo (PMID: 39345555)
summary: Mylpf dosage is necessary for and proportionate to fast-twitch myofibril growth in zebrafish embryos. The two zebrafish Mylpf genes (mylpfa and mylpfb) are exclusively expressed in fast-twitch muscle; mylpfa -/- mutants show severely reduced fast-twitch myofibrils and loss of high-speed movement, while mylpfa -/- ;mylpfb -/- double mutants fail to form myofibrils entirely. Disease-associated MYLPF alleles reduce myofibril size proportionally to protein abundance.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Unsupervised learning revealed metabolic syndrome sub-groups with differing phenotypic and genotypic traits (A. Lim et al.)
summary: MYLPF (rs8054556) is identified as a novel GWAS variant associated with metabolic syndrome cluster C1 (non-descriptive cluster with highest CVD risk). MYLPF is specifically upregulated in skeletal muscle tissue and was unique to the C1 cluster, suggesting a skeletal muscle-specific role in metabolic syndrome pathogenesis.

citation: Bioinformatic Analysis Identifies Potential Key Genes in the Pathogenesis of Turner Syndrome (PMID: 32210915)
sample_size: 26 Turner syndrome patients, 10 normal female controls
summary: MYLPF is identified as a downregulated gene in Turner syndrome (45,XO) patients compared to normal females (46,XX) and is associated with the circulatory system. MYLPF is part of tissue-specific gene expression patterns related to skeletal muscle and circulatory function in TS pathogenesis.

citation: Integrative analysis identifies novel proteins associated with chronic kidney disease in participants with abnormal glucose metabolism (PMID: 40934961)

summary: MYLPF is identified as a novel protein associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in participants with abnormal glucose metabolism through integrated observational and Mendelian randomization analyses. summary: PCBP2 is an RNA-binding protein that binds to PHGDH and is protected from ubiquitination degradation by this interaction. PCBP2 stabilizes SLC7A11 mRNA and increases its expression, thereby inhibiting ferroptosis and promoting bladder cancer progression.

citation: DMT1 and iron transport (PMID: 30055235)
summary: PCBP2 is identified as an iron chaperone that functions in safe transport of ferrous iron in the cytosol, contributing to iron homeostasis and preventing cellular damage from reactive oxygen species.

citation: PCBP2 Mediates Olaparib Resistance in Breast Cancer by Inhibiting m6A Methylation to Stabilize PARP1 mRNA (PMID: 40773674)
summary: PCBP2 is upregulated in olaparib-resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancer cells. PCBP2 directly binds PARP1 mRNA, inhibits m6A methylation, and stabilizes PARP1 mRNA, enhancing DNA repair and conferring resistance to PARP inhibitors.

citation: Acteoside ameliorates hepatocyte ferroptosis and hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury via targeting PCBP2 (PMID: 40486855)
summary: PCBP2 downregulation correlates with hepatocyte ferroptosis and compromises stability of SLC7A11 mRNA. PCBP2 knockdown also facilitates HIF1α-mediated HMGB1 expression and M1 macrophage recruitment. Acteoside enhances PCBP2 binding affinity to system Xc- components and stabilizes Slc3a2/Slc7a11 mRNA.

citation: Role of PCBP2 in regulating nanovesicles loaded with curcumin to mitigate neuroferroptosis in neural damage caused by heat stroke (PMID: 39731111)
summary: Proteomic analysis identified PCBP2 as a key factor through which curcumin-loaded nanovesicles exert neuroprotection against ferroptosis in PC12 cells. PCBP2 stabilizes SLC7A11 mRNA; silencing PCBP2 reverses the protective effects and increases ferroptosis, while SLC7A11 overexpression rescues the phenotype.

citation: FAD synthase confers ferroptosis resistance and restrains CD8+ T cell recruitment in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 41162372)
summary: FADS stabilizes PCBP2 through non-enzymatic function, and this stabilization confers ferroptosis resistance in HCC cells. PCBP2 is implicated in maintaining cellular ferroptosis resistance downstream of FADS.

citation: Pharmacologic inhibition of PCBP2 biomolecular condensates relieves Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 41298370)
summary: PCBP2 elevation in AD brain correlates with biomolecular condensate formation via phase separation. These condensates sequester mitochondrial and mRNA-binding proteins, impairing mitochondrial function and promoting BACE1 mRNA decay. Small molecule CN-0928 inhibits condensates by reducing PCBP2 levels through INTS1 interaction.

citation: RNA binding proteins PCBP1 and PCBP2 regulate pancreatic β cell translation (PMID: 40451383)
summary: PCBP2 and PCBP1 are key post-transcriptional regulators of β cell function. Combined Pcbp1/2 deletion causes severe diabetes with compromised β cell viability. PCBPs co-stabilize mRNAs encoding translation initiation factors and ribosomal proteins through binding and stabilization, sustaining global mRNA translation rates critical for glucose homeostasis.

citation: Circ_0005397 inhibits ferroptosis of pancreatic cancer cells by up-regulating PCBP2 through KAT6A/H3K9Ac (PMID: 39235355)
summary: PCBP2 is highly expressed in pancreatic cancer and positively correlated with circ_0005397. Circ_0005397 promotes PCBP2 transcription by facilitating KAT6A and H3K9ac binding to the PCBP2 promoter. PCBP2 upregulation inhibits ferroptosis; circ_0005397 knockdown sensitizes cells to ferroptosis via PCBP2 downregulation.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Germline whole genome sequencing of children with Down syndrome identifies novel variants associated with risk of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
summary: Whole genome sequencing identified 22 significant variants mapping to PCBP2 associated with Down syndrome-ALL risk (top variant rs1361910621, OR=2.24). PCBP2 is characterized as a poly(rC)-binding protein functioning as a potential oncogenic splicing factor and novel tumor suppressor in hematologic malignancies.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Iron homeostasis modulates the activity of microRNA pathway through PCBP2
summary: PCBP2 is a cytosolic iron chaperone required for RNAi-enhancing activity by metal chelators. PCBP2 associates with Dicer and promotes miRNA precursor processing. Intracellular iron levels modulate PCBP2-Dicer association, PCBP2 multimerization, and its ability to bind miRNA precursors, linking iron metabolism to miRNA pathway regulation.

diagnostic_reason: de novo heterozygous nonsense variant, predicted to cause loss of normal protein function, first reported NLGN2 nonsense variant in humans

citation: Identifying therapeutic target genes for migraine by systematic druggable genome-wide Mendelian randomization (PMID: 38867170)

citation: NLGN1 and NLGN2 in the prefrontal cortex: their role in memory consolidation and strengthening (PMID: 29278843)
summary: NLGN2 is an inhibitory synaptic protein in the prefrontal cortex that regulates memory formation and modulation of memory strength. Changes in NLGN2 expression in inhibitory neuronal subpopulations regulate dynamic processes of memory consolidation and strengthening.

citation: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants (PMID: 35468861)
summary: NLGN2 was identified as a high-confidence (>90% true-positive probability) candidate gene for neurodevelopmental disorders through integrated analysis of de novo SNVs and CNVs in 41,165 individuals with NDDs, based on functional similarity to known NDD genes.

citation: Functional Neuroligin-2-MDGA1 interactions differentially regulate synaptic GABA(A)Rs and cytosolic gephyrin aggregation (PMID: 39284869)

Loss of MDGA1, but not MDGA2, ameliorates abnormal cytosolic gephyrin aggregation and reduction in inhibitory synaptic transmission in NLGN2 knockout mice, indicating MDGA1 modulates NLGN2 function at GABAergic synapses.

citation: Licochalcone A prevents cognitive decline in a lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation mice model (PMID: 39930360)
summary: NLGN2 mRNA expression was significantly reduced in the brains of LPS-treated mice compared to saline controls, and this reduction was associated with memory impairment and depressive-like behavior. LCA treatment protected against LPS-induced downregulation of NLGN2 and other synaptic proteins.

citation: GluN2D Subunit in Parvalbumin Interneurons Regulates Prefrontal Cortex Feedforward Inhibitory Circuit and Molecular Networks Relevant to Schizophrenia (PMID: 37004850)
summary: NLGN2 is involved in formation of inhibitory synapses and was downregulated in PV-GluN2D knockout mice. NLGN2 is part of molecular networks regulating GABAergic synapses and is associated with schizophrenia susceptibility genes.

citation: Expression and structural analysis of human neuroligin 2 and neuroligin 3 implicated in autism spectrum disorders (PMID: 36479216)

summary: NLGN2 and NLGN3 have distinct distributions and functions in synapse development and plasticity. citation: Distinct mechanisms control the specific synaptic functions of Neuroligin 1 and Neuroligin 2 (PMID: 39747663)

citation: ASHG 2018 - Targeted sequencing of postsynaptic protein genes associated with schizophrenia: A role for multiple rare risk mutations in schizophrenia susceptibility (M. Cheng et al.)

citation: Rab14 overexpression regulates gemcitabine sensitivity through regulation of Bcl-2 and mitochondrial function in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 30267303)

RAB14 upregulates mitochondrial membrane potential and Bcl-2 expression while downregulating pro-apoptotic markers (caspase-3, PARP cleavage, cytochrome c release).

citation: Ayte et al. 2000 - Promoter-driven splicing regulation in fission yeast (PMID: 18815595)
summary: Rem1 is a meiosis-specific cyclin in Schizosaccharomyces pombe whose expression is regulated by both transcription and splicing. Rem1 deletion causes decreased intragenic meiotic recombination and delayed onset of meiosis I. Ectopic expression in mitotic cells induces G1 arrest and mitotic catastrophes. Splicing regulation depends on forkhead transcription factors Mei4 (positive regulator) and Fkh2 (negative regulator).

citation: Prakash et al. 1989 - Spontaneous mitotic recombination in yeast: the hyper-recombinational rem1 mutations are alleles of the RAD3 gene (PMID: 2840336)
summary: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, rem1 mutations are alleles of RAD3 that confer high levels of spontaneous mitotic gene conversion, crossing over, and mutation. rem1 strains show distinct genetic interactions with recombination-repair pathway mutations compared to UV-sensitive RAD3 alleles. Double mutants of rem1 with recombination-repair defects are inviable, suggesting rem1 functions in a recombination-repair pathway distinct from UV excision repair.

citation: Ayte et al. 2001 - A meiosis-specific cyclin regulated by splicing is required for proper progression through meiosis (PMID: 16024772)
summary: Rem1 is a fission yeast B-type cyclin present exclusively during meiosis. Rem1-deficient cells show impaired meiotic recombination and require Rem1 for premeiotic DNA synthesis when Cig2 is absent. Rem1 splicing is positively regulated by Mei4 and negatively by Cig2, ensuring timely cyclin appearance during meiotic progression.

citation: Omelchenko et al. 2013 - Adrenergic signaling controls RGK-dependent trafficking of cardiac voltage-gated L-type Ca2+ channels through PKD1 (PMID: 22076634)
summary: Rem1, a member of the RGK (Rad-Gem/Kir-related) GTPase family, is strongly and specifically expressed in cardiac tissue. Phosphorylation of Rem1 at Ser18 by protein kinase D1 (downstream of α1-adrenergic signaling) relieves Rem1-mediated inhibition of voltage-gated L-type calcium channels, increasing channel activity and plasma membrane expression in neonatal cardiomyocytes and adult ventricular myocytes.

citation: Liang et al. 2020 - Ras associated with diabetes may play a role in fracture nonunion development in rats (PMID: 31830958)
summary: Rem1, an RGK subfamily member, was analyzed alongside Rad in rat fracture healing models. Real-time PCR showed Rad expression increased significantly in nonunions versus standard healing fractures at post-fracture days 14, 21, and 28. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed similar immunolocalization patterns of Rad and Rem1 in both fracture types at days 14 and 21.

citation: Yamaguchi et al. 2010 - Rapid Oligo-Galacturonide Induced Changes in Protein Phosphorylation in Arabidopsis (PMID: 26811356)
summary: REM1.3, a putative scaffold protein, was identified as a phosphoprotein with rapid OG-induced phosphorylation changes in Arabidopsis. Genetic analysis showed that null mutations in REM1.3 enhance a dominant WAK allele, indicating REM1.3 plays a role in the oligo-galacturonide-induced cell wall stress response pathway.

citation: Cerutti et al. 2011 - REM1, a new type of long terminal repeat retrotransposon in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (PMID: 16287873)
summary: CrREM1 is a Ty3-gypsy-related LTR retrotransposon identified in the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. It is present in low copy number, highly methylated, and exhibits inducible transpositional activity. CrREM1 amplifies copy number during foreign DNA integration and genetic crosses but shows restricted integration despite high transcriptional activity, suggesting a regulatory mechanism to minimize genomic damage.

citation: Tanaka et al. 2000 - Negative control contributes to an extensive program of meiotic splicing in fission yeast (PMID: 15893732)
summary: Rem1 is one of two cyclins (along with crs1) identified as meiotically spliced transcripts in Schizosaccharomyces pombe that retain introns during vegetative growth. Splicing regulation occurs via inhibition in mitotic cells rather than positive activation, with regulatory sequences located outside coding regions far from target introns.

citation: Scheffzek et al. 2007 - Biochemical and structural characterization of the gem GTPase (PMID: 17107948)
summary: Rem1 is a member of the RGK protein family (Rad, Gem, Rem1, Rem2) that constitute an atypical branch of the Ras superfamily. RGK proteins exhibit lower GDP/GTP binding affinities (micromolar range) compared to H-Ras, higher GTPase activity regulated by N- and C-terminal extensions, and carry bulky DXWEX motifs in switch II that affect nucleotide binding and regulation.

citation: Tian et al. 2024 - Mining of Root-Specific Expression Genes and Their Core Cis-Regulatory Elements in Plants (PMID: 40004183)
sample_size: 489 RTEGs in Arabidopsis, 276 in rice, 728 in maize; 34 conserved across three species

citation: Chicken sine oculis binding protein homolog (sobp), a novel gene that may regulate feather development. (PMID: 22802190)

citation: SPTSSA variants alter sphingolipid synthesis and cause a complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (PMID: 36718090)

summary: Two pathogenic SPTSSA variants (missense and frameshift) impaired negative regulation of serine palmitoyltransferase by ORMDLs, leading to excessive sphingolipid synthesis. citation: SPTSSA Is a Prognostic Marker for Glioblastoma Associated with Tumor-Infiltrating Immune Cells and Oxidative Stress (PMID: 36062185)

significance: p<0.05 for upregulation and survival association
summary: SPTSSA expression was significantly upregulated in diffuse glioma compared to normal tissues and associated with poor survival. SPTSSA expression enriched in oxidative stress-related GO terms and was significantly associated with tumor-infiltrating immune cells and overall survival.

citation: Human Rhinovirus Infection of the Respiratory Tract Affects Sphingolipid Synthesis (PMID: 34851798)

summary: Two de novo missense variants (p.Thr51Ile) and one homozygous frameshift variant (p.Gln58AlafsTer10) in SPTSSA impaired ORMDL-mediated feedback inhibition of SPT, causing excessive sphingolipid synthesis. citation: The Neuromuscular Junction and Wide Heterogeneity of Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes (PMID: 29874875)
summary: SLC18A3 mutations cause congenital myasthenic syndromes (CMS) by impairing acetylcholine recycling and synthesis. citation: SLC18A3 promoted renal cancer development through acetylcholine/cAMP signaling (PMID: 36225635)

summary: SLC18A3 (vesicular acetylcholine transporter) is upregulated in renal cancer patients and enhances acetylcholine uptake into cancer cells. SLC18A3 overexpression in A489 tumor-bearing mice caused sustained tumor growth and increased lung metastases.

citation: SLC18: Vesicular neurotransmitter transporters for monoamines and acetylcholine (PMID: 23506877)
summary: SLC18A3 is the vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) that mediates active transport of acetylcholine into synaptic vesicles for exocytotic release. SLC18A3 is a member of the SLC18 family within the Drug:H+ Antiporter-1 Family (DHA1) and Major Facilitator Superfamily (MFS).

summary: SLC18A3 expression in urinary bladder is significantly altered by microbiota status, with differential expression between germ-free and specific pathogen-free mice. SLC18A3 is part of the neuromuscular synaptic transmission gene set that is regulated by microbiota composition.

summary: SLC18A3 expression is significantly altered in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients and identified as a possible biomarker for severe OSA. citation: RYR2-ryanodinopathies: from calcium overload to calcium deficiency (PMID: 37387319)

RYR2 mutations represent distinct cardiac ryanodinopathies with different pathophysiological mechanisms.

citation: Ero1α-Dependent ERp44 Dissociation From RyR2 Contributes to Cardiac Arrhythmia (PMID: 35086342)

summary: RYR2 forms a redox-sensitive intraluminal complex with ERp44 mediated by cysteine 4806. Ero1α inhibition stabilizes the RYR2-ERp44 complex, reducing proarrhythmic calcium waves and ventricular tachyarrhythmias in hypertrophic hearts.

citation: Ryanodine receptor 2 (RYR2) dysfunction activates the unfolded protein response and perturbs cardiomyocyte maturation (PMID: 35576474)

summary: RYR2 depletion in cardiomyocytes triggers ER stress pathway activation through ATF4, impairing cardiomyocyte maturation. RYR2 regulates ER homeostasis essential for proper cardiomyocyte development. ER stress alleviator tauroursodeoxycholic acid partially rescues RYR2-depletion defects, and ATF4 overexpression recapitulates maturation defects.

citation: Foxp3-mediated blockage of ryanodine receptor 2 underlies contact-based suppression by regulatory T cells (PMID: 38099494)

summary: Foxp3 transcription factor blocks RYR2 transcription in regulatory T cells, reducing basal calcium oscillations and m-calpain activities required for T cell disengagement from dendritic cells. RYR2 deficiency renders CD4+ T cells immune suppressive and phenotypically similar to Foxp3+ Tregs, revealing RYR2-mediated calcium signaling as a central effector mechanism of Treg immune suppression.

citation: Astrocyte-derived SerpinA3N promotes neuroinflammation and epileptic seizures by activating the NF-κB signaling pathway in mice with temporal lobe epilepsy (PMID: 37422673)
sample_size: Kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy mouse model
summary: SerpinA3N interacts with RYR2 and promotes RYR2 phosphorylation in astrocytes during kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy. SerpinA3N-RYR2 interaction contributes to seizure-induced neuroinflammation through NF-κB pathway activation. This represents a novel mechanism linking RYR2 to seizure pathogenesis beyond cardiac function.

citation: MBD2 regulates the progression and chemoresistance of cholangiocarcinoma through interaction with WDR5 (PMID: 39350229)

citation: The MYC-WDR5 Nexus and Cancer (PMID: 26383167)
summary: WDR5, a WD40-repeat protein component of chromatin-regulatory complexes, interacts with MYC oncoproteins to regulate target gene recognition and selection. citation: Fibroblast-specific PRMT5 deficiency suppresses cardiac fibrosis and left ventricular dysfunction in male mice (PMID: 38503742)
summary: WDR5/MLL1 methyltransferase complex mediates H3K4 tri-methylation that recognizes PRMT5-mediated H3R2 dimethylation at the α-SMA promoter in cardiac fibroblasts. citation: Wdr5-mediated H3K4 methylation facilitates HSPC development via maintenance of genomic stability in zebrafish (PMID: 40112113)
summary: Loss of wdr5 in zebrafish embryos led to severe reduction of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) pool with attenuated H3K4 methylation and p53-dependent apoptosis. Wdr5-mediated H3K4 methylation maintains genomic stability by inhibiting abnormal R-loop formation and activating DNA damage response pathways essential for HSPC survival during rapid proliferation.

citation: NSUN5 Facilitates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Increasing SMAD3 Expression (PMID: 39531371)
summary: NSUN5 promotes enrichment of H3K4me3 at the SMAD3 promoter through recruitment of WDR5, facilitating HCC metastasis via SMAD3-mediated EMT pathways. This demonstrates WDR5's role as a component recruited to specific promoters to establish activating histone marks in cancer progression.

citation: WDR5 represents a therapeutically exploitable target for cancer stem cells in glioblastoma (PMID: 36732025)
summary: WDR5 is a component of the WRAD complex essential for maintaining glioblastoma cancer stem cells (CSCs). citation: ASHG 2017 - Epigenetic regulation of the Runx2 gene in lung cancer
summary: WDR5 is part of the WDR5/MLL/UTX complex that regulates Runx2 gene expression through covalent histone modifications. phenotype: Reduced NCC phosphorylation in distal convoluted tubule; Activation of compensatory response; Altered Na+ reabsorption in kidney
