phenotype: Histologically confirmed focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS); Non-functional WNK4 develops FSGS phenotype

citation: Regulation of the WNK4-SPAK-NCC pathway by the calcium-sensing receptor (PMID: 37530086)
summary: WNK4 is a key component of the CaSR-WNK4-SPAK-NCC signaling pathway in the distal convoluted tubule. CaSR activation stimulates PKC-dependent WNK4 signaling, which activates SPAK and increases NCC activity to recover NaCl reabsorption. Glucose and fructose enhance this pathway, contributing to hypertension in diabetic patients.

citation: WNK4 kinase: from structure to physiology (PMID: 33491560)
summary: WNK4 is a serine-threonine kinase with atypical catalytic lysine positioning that functions as a positive regulator of the thiazide-sensitive NCC in the distal convoluted tubule. Gain-of-function mutations in WNK4 cause familial hyperkalemic hypertension through increased NCC activation and impaired renal K+ secretion. WNK4 function is regulated at multiple levels and responds to various physiological conditions.

citation: WNK4 kinase: role of chloride sensing in the distal convoluted tubule (PMID: 33394730)
summary: WNK4 functions as a physiological intracellular chloride sensor in the DCT with the highest chloride sensitivity among WNK kinases. Chloride-insensitive WNK4 mice develop hypertension with increased NCC activity, proving WNK4 is inhibitable by physiological [Cl-]i. This chloride-sensing mechanism is responsible for hypokalemia-induced NCC activation and explains the inverse relationship between dietary potassium intake and NCC activity.

citation: Dysregulation of the WNK4-SPAK/OSR1 pathway has a minor effect on baseline NKCC2 phosphorylation (PMID: 37881876)
sample_size: Multiple transgenic mouse lines on C57BL/6 background
summary: Using C57BL/6-specific phospho-NKCC2 antibodies in knockout mice (Wnk4-/-, Osr1-/-, Spak-/-, Osr1-/-/Spak-/-) and familial hyperkalemic hypertension models, WNK4-SPAK/OSR1 pathway disruption strongly reduces NCC phosphorylation but only mildly affects NKCC2 phosphorylation, suggesting other kinases regulate NKCC2. In FHHt models, NKCC2 phosphorylation remains unchanged despite elevated WNK4 abundance.

citation: Glucose/Fructose Delivery to the Distal Nephron Activates the Sodium-Chloride Cotransporter via the Calcium-Sensing Receptor (PMID: 36288902)
sample_size: HEK-293 cells, C57BL/6 mice, WNK4-KO mice, ex vivo rat kidneys, healthy human volunteers
summary: In HEK-293 cells, glucose/fructose exposure increased SPAK phosphorylation in a WNK4- and CaSR-dependent manner. In C57BL/6 and WNK4-knockout mice, fructose or dapagliflozin-induced glycosuria activated the WNK4-SPAK-NCC pathway in a CaSR-dependent manner, demonstrating WNK4's role in glucose/fructose-mediated NCC activation.

citation: Life and death of the distal nephron: WNK4 and NCC as major players (PMID: 17084706)
summary: WNK4 missense mutations cause familial hyperkalemic hypertension. In vitro studies show WNK4 regulates surface expression and activity of multiple ion channels and transporters. Transgenic mouse models demonstrate WNK4 controls ion handling in the kidney mainly through regulation of NCC activity.

citation: WNK1 and WNK4, new players in salt and water homeostasis (PMID: 15639021)
summary: WNK4 is a serine-threonine kinase highly expressed in kidney and chloride-transporting epithelia. In the renal distal tubule, WNK4 inhibits sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion via inhibition of NCC and ROMK activity. FHH mutations in WNK4 lead to loss of NCC inhibition and increased ROMK inhibition, and increase paracellular chloride permeability in MDCK cells.

citation: WNK4-mediated regulation of renal ion transport proteins (PMID: 17634397)
sample_size: Xenopus laevis oocytes, transgenic and knockin mice
summary: WNK4 point mutations are linked to familial hyperkalemic hypertension. WNK4 regulates multiple ion transport proteins (Na+, K+, Ca2+, Cl-) and claudins in the distal nephron through altered plasma membrane abundance. WNK4 activates stress-related kinases to regulate SLC12 family cation-chloride cotransporters, with FHH-causing mutants showing altered regulation patterns.

citation: KLHL3-dependent WNK4 degradation affected by potassium through the neddylation and autophagy pathway (PMID: 37481568)
sample_size: HEK293 cells, mice on low/high potassium diets
summary: In HEK293 cells and mice, low potassium increases WNK4 abundance and phosphorylation through impaired KLHL3-dependent degradation via neddylation and autophagy pathways. MLN4924 (neddylation inhibitor) and autophagy inhibitors increase WNK4 levels, demonstrating potassium-dependent regulation of WNK4 stability relevant to familial hyperkalemic hypertension.

citation: ASHG 2017 - Statistical framework for biological interpretation and improvement of genetic association studies (M. Artomov et al.)
sample_size: FSGS genetic association study with network analysis
significance: Posterior p-value significant after permutation testing; >10 fold improvement in association signal
summary: WNK4 was identified in a protein-protein network analysis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) genetic association data with >10-fold improvement in association signal. Mouse models demonstrated that non-functional WNK4 develops histologically confirmed FSGS, proving WNK4's causal role in FSGS pathogenesis.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Two new genes for dominant and recessive pseudohypoaldosteronism type II provide novel insights into regulation of serum potassium, pH, and blood pressure (L.M. Boyden et al.)
summary: WNK4 mutations cause dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type II (PHAII) characterized by impaired potassium and acid excretion, increased renal salt reabsorption, and hypertension ameliorated by thiazide diuretics. WNK4 is expressed in the distal nephron and regulates NCCT and other mediators of ion flux, functioning as part of a molecular switch for kidney's response to potassium excess and volume depletion.

phenotype: moderate intellectual disability; atypical autism; attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; behavioral disturbances; developmental delays in motor and verbal skills
diagnostic_reason: de novo variant in highly conserved helicase motif of UPF1; comparison with three previously reported UPF1 variants showing similar neurodevelopmental phenotypes

phenotype: intellectual disabilities; similar dysmorphic features to Patient 1
diagnostic_reason: de novo variants identified by trio exome analysis; functional validation in Drosophila models demonstrated deleterious effects with developmental lethality at different stages

phenotype: Altered endogenous transcript levels of appa, appb, aplp1, and aplp2; Regulation of APP family member expression levels; Involvement in degradation of mutant mRNA with PTC

phenotype: Hyperactivated NMD during cerebral cortex development; Hyperactivated NMD during hippocampus development; Hyperactivated NMD during cerebellum development; Abnormal regulation of neuronal mRNAs important for brain development

phenotype: Spontaneous lung adenocarcinoma; Insufficient histone supply; Chromatin relaxation; Genomic instability; Increased rate of gene mutations; Malignant transformation

citation: Structure-Mediated RNA Decay by UPF1 and G3BP1 (PMID: 32017897)
summary: UPF1 is a core component of a genome-wide RNA decay pathway that reduces mRNA half-lives based on 3' UTR secondary structure. Depletion of UPF1 increased steady-state levels of mRNAs with highly structured 3' UTRs and structured circular RNAs, demonstrating UPF1's role in structure-dependent mRNA degradation independent of sequence specificity.

citation: Cellular functions of eukaryotic RNA helicases and their links to human diseases (PMID: 37474727)
summary: UPF1 is classified as an Upf1-like RNA helicase that uses ATP hydrolysis to bind and remodel RNA and RNA-protein complexes. UPF1 is involved in virtually all aspects of eukaryotic RNA metabolism including transcription regulation, pre-mRNA splicing, ribosome assembly, translation, and RNA decay pathways.

citation: CRISPR/Cas9 screen reveals that targeting TRIM34 enhances ferroptosis sensitivity and augments immunotherapy efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 38704136)
summary: TRIM34 directly interacts with UPF1 to promote its ubiquitination and degradation in HCC cells. TRIM34-mediated degradation of UPF1 suppresses GPX4 transcript degradation via the NMD pathway, promoting ferroptosis resistance. This demonstrates UPF1's role as a core NMD component whose stability is regulated by E3 ligase-mediated ubiquitination.

citation: Translation-coupled mRNA quality control mechanisms (PMID: 37605642)
summary: UPF1 is a core trans-acting factor in the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway, a translation-coupled mRNA quality control mechanism that eliminates mRNAs with premature termination codons. Recent mechanistic findings and novel factors in NMD regulation are reviewed with emphasis on UPF1's central role.

citation: Interaction Between LncRNA and UPF1 in Tumors (PMID: 33732285)
summary: UPF1 is a key RNA-binding protein that interacts with long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to regulate gene expression and control RNA decay. UPF1 expression is often dysregulated in tumors, and lncRNA-UPF1 interactions provide a fundamental basis for cell transformation and tumorigenic growth.

citation: MET Amplification Attenuates Lung Tumor Response to Immunotherapy by Inhibiting STING (PMID: 34099454)
sample_size: 81 lung cancer patients; single-cell RNA-seq of >20,000 immune cells
summary: Oncogenic MET signaling induces phosphorylation of UPF1, which then downregulates STING expression by modulating the 3'-UTR length of STING mRNA through NMD. This demonstrates UPF1's role in post-transcriptional regulation of immune-related genes and its regulation by kinase signaling pathways.

citation: Staufen-mediated mRNA decay (PMID: 23681777)
summary: UPF1 is a key SMD (Staufen-mediated mRNA decay) factor that directly interacts with STAU1 and STAU2 double-stranded RNA-binding proteins, which enhance UPF1's helicase activity to promote mRNA decay. SMD and NMD are competitive pathways that both employ UPF1, with implications for cellular differentiation.

citation: Advances in molecular function of UPF1 in Cancer (PMID: 38621446)
summary: UPF1 is a master regulator of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) that prevents synthesis of C-terminally truncated proteins from mRNAs with premature termination codons. UPF1 may also function as an E3 ligase to degrade target proteins independently of mRNA decay mechanisms, and low UPF1 expression correlates with poor cancer prognosis.

citation: ADAR1-HNRNPL-Mediated CircCANX Decline Promotes Autophagy in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (PMID: 40091520)
sample_size: COPD patient samples and in vitro/in vivo models
summary: CircCANX recruits UPF1 and P53 mRNA to form a ternary complex that mediates P53 mRNA degradation through the NMD pathway in COPD. This demonstrates UPF1's role in NMD-mediated degradation of specific mRNA targets and its involvement in disease-relevant regulatory mechanisms.

citation: UPF1 deficiency enhances mitochondrial ROS which promotes an immunosuppressive microenvironment in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PMID: 40591563)
sample_size: KPC mouse-derived pancreatic cancer cells; orthotopic implantation in C57BL/6 mice
summary: UPF1 deficiency in pancreatic cancer cells increases mitochondrial complex I activity and ROS production, leading to elevated inflammatory cytokine secretion (G-CSF, CXCL2) that recruits myeloid-derived suppressor cells and suppresses anti-tumor immunity. This reveals a non-canonical role for UPF1 in regulating mitochondrial metabolism and immune suppression.

citation: ASHG 2023 - An adult male with UPF1-related neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: not provided)
significance: Variant classified as Likely Pathogenic per ACMG guidelines
summary: A de novo UPF1 variant (c.1846 A>G, p.Thr616Ala) causes neurodevelopmental disorder with infantile hypotonia, global developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, myoclonic epilepsy, and overgrowth features. This is only the third reported case of UPF1-related neurodevelopmental disorder, expanding the phenotypic spectrum and suggesting disruption of the NMD pathway causes neurological disease.

citation: ASHG 2017 - The mechanism and function of targeting lincRNAs by NMD in mammals (PMID: not provided)
summary: UPF1 directly targets long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) for NMD-mediated degradation, with 11.27% of lincRNAs affected by NMD. NMD-targeted lincRNAs are more lowly expressed and less conserved than other lincRNAs, suggesting they represent expression noise rather than functional products.

citation: ASHG 2016 - The SMN1 mutation c.22-23 insA causes spinal muscular atrophy by nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (PMID: not provided)
sample_size: SMA patient-derived immortalized B-lymphoblasts and fibroblasts
significance: 22-fold increase in SMN1 mRNA with puromycin; 10-fold with cycloheximide; 4-fold with UPF1 knockdown
summary: UPF1 knockdown in patient-derived fibroblasts carrying an SMN1 frameshift mutation rescues SMN1 mRNA and protein levels, demonstrating that the mutation triggers NMD-mediated degradation. NMD inhibition by puromycin and cycloheximide increased SMN1 mRNA levels up to 22-fold, confirming UPF1's central role in NMD-dependent pathogenesis of SMA.

citation: ASHG 2012 - A nonsense mutation in DHTKD1 causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 in a large Chinese pedigree (PMID: not provided)
sample_size: 5-generation family with 8 affected individuals; 250 unrelated controls
significance: DHTKD1 mRNA reduced to 50% in patient peripheral blood; rescued by UPF1 silencing
summary: UPF1 silencing rescues decreased levels of mutant DHTKD1 mRNA and protein in cells transfected with a nonsense mutation, demonstrating that NMD-mediated degradation causes disease. This shows UPF1's role in recognizing and degrading mRNAs with premature termination codons in the context of inherited neuropathy.

phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; autism
diagnostic_reason: Patient mutations altering translational activity of ZNF644 in neurons; identified through massively parallel reporter assay and confirmed in patient-derived cell lines to alter protein production

phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: Functional 5'UTR mutations from NDD families identified through polysome-MPRA and Cre-dependent MPRA assays; mutations alter translational activity and protein production

phenotype: Altered G9a/H3K9me2-mediated gene silencing during neurogenesis; Defects in retinal differentiation; Impaired transition of proliferating progenitor cells toward differentiation; Complementary roles of znf644a and znf644b in regulating progenitor gene expression

phenotype: Increased vitreous chamber depth; Altered lens diameter; High myopia phenotype; Preserved retinal physiological function
significance: significant difference in vitreous chamber depth and lens diameter

citation: G9a and ZNF644 Physically Associate to Suppress Progenitor Gene Expression during Neurogenesis (PMID: 27546533)
summary: ZNF644 is identified as a G9a/GLP-interacting protein that co-regulates histone methylation. In zebrafish, znf644a and znf644b orthologs have complementary roles in regulating G9a/H3K9me2-mediated gene silencing during neurogenesis and retinal differentiation, functioning as critical co-regulators of G9a/H3K9me2-mediated gene silencing during neuronal differentiation.

citation: The zinc finger proteins ZNF644 and WIZ regulate the G9a/GLP complex for gene repression (PMID: 25789554)
summary: ZNF644 is identified as a core subunit of the G9a/GLP complex through unbiased protein affinity purification. ZNF644 contains multiple zinc finger motifs that recognize consensus DNA sequences and targets G9a to chromatin to mediate H3K9 methylation and gene repression.

citation: Mutational screening of AGRN, SLC39A5, SCO2, P4HA2, BSG, ZNF644, and CPSF1 in a Chinese cohort of 103 patients with nonsyndromic high myopia (PMID: 35002215)
summary: A heterozygous variant c.3266A>G, p.Y1089C in ZNF644 was identified in one of 103 high myopia patients. Bioinformatics analysis supported the potential pathogenicity of this variant, providing evidence for ZNF644's role in high myopia inheritance.

citation: Study of a US cohort supports the role of ZNF644 and high-grade myopia susceptibility (PMID: 22539872)
summary: Two novel ZNF644 variants (c.725C>T, c.821A>T) were identified in high-grade myopia cases from a US cohort (one Caucasian, one African American), not found in 672 ethnically matched controls. A rare variant rs12117237 (c.2119A>G) with 0.2% minor allele frequency was present in 6 cases and 5 controls.

citation: Mutational investigation of 17 causative genes in a cohort of 113 families with nonsyndromic early-onset high myopia in northwestern China (PMID: 36964802)
summary: Multiple ZNF644 variants were identified in high myopia families: novel variants c.3214C>A/p.H1072N and c.2195C>T/p.A732V, and rare variants c.1100C>T/p.P367L, c.2014A>G/p.S672G, and c.3261A>C/p.E1087D. Ten variants co-segregated with high myopia, providing evidence that ZNF644 contributes to hereditable high myopia.

citation: Downregulation of circ-ZNF644 alleviates LPS-induced HK2 cell injury via miR-335-5p/HIPK1 axis (PMID: 36052886)
sample_size: sepsis-induced AKI patients and HK2 cell culture
summary: Circular RNA derived from ZNF644 (circ-ZNF644) was overexpressed in sepsis-induced acute kidney injury patients. In LPS-stimulated HK2 kidney cells, circ-ZNF644 knockdown suppressed cell injury, inflammation, and apoptosis through sponging miR-335-5p and regulating HIPK1 expression.

citation: CircZNF644 aggravates lipopolysaccharide-induced HK-2 cell impairment via the miR-140-5p/MLKL axis (PMID: 35976517)
summary: CircZNF644 was upregulated in LPS-stimulated HK-2 kidney cells. CircZNF644 knockdown reversed LPS-mediated inhibition of cell proliferation and cell cycle progression, and reduced apoptosis and inflammation through the miR-140-5p/MLKL pathway.

citation: miR-362 regulates the proliferation and apoptosis of porcine immature Sertoli cells through targeting the ZNF644 gene (PMID: 30021720)
summary: ZNF644 is a direct target of miR-362 in porcine immature Sertoli cells. Over-expression of miR-362 or knockdown of ZNF644 arrested cells in G1/G2 phases, inhibited proliferation, and enhanced apoptosis, indicating ZNF644 regulates Sertoli cell proliferation and survival.

citation: Developing ZNF Gene Signatures Predicting Radiosensitivity of Patients with Breast Cancer (PMID: 34504527)
sample_size: 976 breast cancer samples from TCGA, validation in METABRIC
summary: High expression of ZNF644 was associated with radiosensitivity in breast cancer patients. A 4-gene signature including ZNF644 (high expression) and three other ZNF genes (low expression) predicted better overall survival on radiotherapy in 976 TCGA breast cancer samples, validated in METABRIC database.

citation: Metabolic, transcriptomic, and proteomic adaptations in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma-patient derived xenograft models across serial passages (PMID: 40605042)
summary: ZNF644 was identified as one of five consistently altered proteins across serial passages of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma PDX models, indicative of enhanced signal transduction and cell cycle regulation during tumor evolution.
